input.prompt:
Live animatronic bear "Frankie" at Clovis Community College STEM day, outdoors, show running NOW (prod). Deadline 20 minutes. Build ONE new independent script /home/spauly/tony-tests/polyglot.py (run with /home/spauly/Desktop/barnaby/evil-autonomous-bear-proj/.venv/bin/python -u) that randomly, every 25–45 s, says ONE of:
(a) a 2-sentence lecture on Dijkstra's algorithm out of the blue (sassy professor-bear tone; write ~12 varied, CORRECT 2-sentence explanations: greedy, priority queue/min-heap, non-negative weights, relaxation, O((V+E) log V), shortest-path tree, why negative edges break it, etc.), spoken in English;
(b) a short line (≤ 12 words) in a random language: Arabic, Chinese (Mandarin), Russian, English, German, or Japanese in a HIGH-PITCHED BABY voice. Lines are Halloween/self-aware bear jokes; write them natively in each language (correct script: العربية, 中文, русский, Deutsch, 日本語), ~6 per language.
Voices: Piper voices live in /home/spauly/tony-tests/voices (en_GB-alan-medium, ru_RU-dmitri-medium already there). Download what's missing from https://huggingface.co/rhasspy/piper-voices/resolve/main/<lang>/<locale>/<name>/<quality>/<file>.onnx (+ .onnx.json), e.g. ar/ar_JO/kareem/medium, zh/zh_CN/huayan/medium, de/de_DE/thorsten/medium. Check that each works with `from piper import PiperVoice` (see /home/spauly/tony-tests/frankie_voice.py _voice/_synth for how it's used). Piper has no Japanese voice as far as I know — verify; if none, use `espeak-ng -v ja` (check it's installed and actually produces Japanese, else fall back to the en_GB voice reading romaji), then make it baby-like: sox pitch +700, tempo 0.85. Apply a light shared chain to everything (highpass 150, compand, equalizer 2800 +6, gain -n -1) — outdoor-loud, a bit distorted (overdrive 3 6).
QUEUE: before playing, take the shared speaker lock exactly like /home/spauly/tony-tests/scene_cam.py speak() does (fcntl.flock on /home/spauly/tony-tests/.speak.lock, then wait until `pgrep -x pw-play` is false, up to 30 s; drop if stale > 45 s), then pw-play. Never talk over others. Render BEFORE taking the lock.
Log to /home/spauly/tony-tests/polyglot.log. Stop file: /home/spauly/tony-tests/NO_POLY.
Also add polyglot to /home/spauly/tony-tests/guardian.sh following the same pattern as dance_loop there (pgrep pattern '^[^ ]*python -u [^ ]*polyglot[.]py$', start via (cd ~/Desktop/barnaby/evil-autonomous-bear-proj && setsid nohup "$PY" -u "$T/polyglot.py" ...)); back up guardian.sh first (.guardian.sh.bak-poly), bash -n it. Do NOT restart the guardian (main session does).
Test: py_compile; render one line per language + one Dijkstra line into the scratchpad /tmp/claude-1000/-home-spauly/74003cd9-c50a-51a5-9802-e3e4aeab6b8f/scratchpad/ and check durations; play at most 2 through the lock (one Japanese baby, one Dijkstra). Don't edit frankie*.py, scene_cam.py, boot.sh, ~/Desktop/barnaby; don't kill any process; no GPIO; no camera. Report: voices used per language, sample lines, and "ready to start".
